compare.title: Comparison
compare.lead: Our composer's drawing beside KAGE's composition of the same IDS: unencoded headwords from the HDIC KRM database, common-use kanji, and characters from earlier review sheets.
compare.dataset: {total} sequences · {krm} unencoded headwords, {joyo} common kanji, {review} review characters · measured {date}
compare.method.label: How these were measured
compare.method.body: The gallery shows {krm} unencoded headwords composed by both sides from the IDS, {joyo} common kanji designed on both sides, and {review} review characters from earlier han-compose sheets. Both drawings were rasterized at 256 px. F1@4 is the harmonic mean of the share of each drawing's ink within 4 px of the other; IoU counts exact ink overlap; layout is the L1 distance between the two 3×3 ink-share grids. For common kanji, 17 have a whole glyph on both sides and three (海, 急, 曜) are composed by this site, so their scores include composition.
compare.method.caveat: KAGE is a reference style, not ground truth. Our typeface is heavier — 1.58× the ink at the median — which lowers IoU and F1; designed glyphs can also differ in variant and stroke design. The layout figure and the drawings show the structural differences.
compare.filter.label: Structure
compare.sort.label: Order
compare.credit: KAGE drawings: zi.tools composes the description from GlyphWiki parts and KAGE renders it.
compare.license: GlyphWiki data is free to use; the KAGE engine is GPL-3.0. The drawings are a snapshot of the run.
compare.operators: Sequences are written in IDS; the boxed symbols are its operators: left-right, above-below, three across, three down and enclosures.
compare.set.label: Set
compare.joyoNote: Most common kanji are designed on both sides; 海, 急 and 曜 are composed by this site, so their scores include composition. The remaining comparisons are type style and variant choice.
compare.reviewNote: Review characters come from earlier han-compose review sheets; some are rare or experimental forms. Both sides draw them from the IDS.
